preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A proposal the user already started, dismissed or let expire is reported back (a dismissed or expired proposal's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

"offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

content.description: The step, as a short imperative phrase (≤7 words).

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list. Use on the first call and whenever the plan changes.

advance.description: true: the in_progress step is done and the next pending step starts (the cheap, usual update).

done.description: 1-based numbers of steps just completed (out-of-order updates).

start.description: 1-based number of the step now in progress (with done, for out-of-order updates).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

schema.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# Alloq

Ressourcen- und Kapazitätsplanung für Softwareteams. Dieses Design System ist aus dem Code der Anwendung abgeleitet: `assets/css/alloq-theme.css`, `app/styles.py`, das Mantine-Theme in `app/app.py` und die Komponenten unter `components/` und `app/components/`. Die UI läuft auf Reflex mit Mantine (`appkit_mantine`). Das Theme legt die eigenen `--alloq-*` Variablen und umgefärbte Mantine-Paletten über die Standardwerte.

## Content Fundamentals

- **Sprache:** Deutsch, sachlich, kurze Wörter. Navigation, Buttons, Status und Meldungen sind deutsch: „Ressourcenplanung“, „Projekt anlegen“, „Abbrechen“, „Keine offenen Risiken.“
- **Titel:** kurze Substantive („Feiertage“, „Projekt Details“). Darüber ein Breadcrumb, darunter höchstens ein Satz Beschreibung.
- **Buttons:** Verb oder Verb mit Objekt. Die Hauptaktion eines Modals nennt das Objekt: „Projekt speichern“.
- **Kennzahlen:** Labels in Versalien („AUSLASTUNG“, „PT FREI“), die Zahl ist die Aussage.
- **Zahlen und Daten:** deutsches Format. Beträge „480.000 €“, kurz „1,2M €“ oder „850T €“. Daten „TT.MM.JJJJ“ oder „1. Sep 2026“. Kalenderwochen „KW 42“. Personentage „PT“.
- **Leere Zustände** sagen, was fehlt, mit Punkt am Ende.
- Keine Ausrufezeichen, keine Emojis.

## Visual Foundations

- **Ton:** warm und ruhig. Ein cremeweißer Grund (`bg-base`) trägt einen weichen Verlauf aus Gold, Salbeigrün, Lavendel und Teal. Im dunklen Modus wird der Grund zu tiefem Petrol (`#141e21`) mit dunklen Blau-, Grün- und Violetttönen.
- **Farbe:** Die Mantine-Primärpalette ist `alloqTeal` (Stufe 6 hell, 7 dunkel). Teal ist die Handlungsfarbe (`primary-filled`, `nav-active-bg`). Gold (`warm-*`, Palette `alloqWarm`) ist die Markenfarbe für Flächen und die Radix-Akzente, nie für kleinen Text. Salbei, Gelb, Terrakotta und Rot tragen Status. Alle Mantine-Paletten außer Violett sind auf diese gedämpften Töne umgefärbt.
- **Flächen:** Karten sind halbtransparent (`fade-bg`, `surface`) und lassen den Verlauf durchscheinen. Modale, Drawer, Tabellenköpfe und das Planungsraster sind deckend (`surface-muted`, `surface-solid`).
- **Rahmen statt Schatten:** Linien in blassem Grün (`border`). Schatten nur für schwebende Elemente (`shadow-soft`), Formularabschnitte und die Modal-Fußzeile.
- **Radien:** `radius-sm` für Tabellen, Raster und Balken, `radius-md` für Eingaben und Buttons, `radius-lg` für Karten, Modale und Drawer, `radius-xl` für Badges und Fortschrittsbalken.
- **Typografie:** Roboto Flex für alles, Roboto Mono für Code, Major Mono Display nur für das Wortzeichen. Seitentitel sind sehr leicht (280, 3rem), Kennzahlen kräftig (700), Namen in Karten 800.
- **Daten:** Tabellenziffern in Rastern und Tabellen. Die aktuelle Woche ist golden hinterlegt (`current-week`).
- **Bewegung:** nur Hintergrundübergänge von 120 bis 200ms bei Hover und ein Skelett-Schimmer beim Laden.

## Iconography

Lucide über `rx.icon`, Strichstärke 1.5px (gesetzt in `base_style`). Größen: 20px in Buttons der Größe `md` und in der Navigation, 16px in Feldern und Kartentiteln, 14px in kleinen Aktionen, 48px in leeren Zuständen. Icons tragen die Textfarbe ihrer Umgebung. Icon-Schaltflächen haben immer ein `aria-label` und einen Tooltip. Die Vorschauen laden die genutzten Lucide-Pfade aus `icons/lucide.js` (aus `lucide-react` 1.26.0).

## Usage Rules

1. Text in `text` oder `text-muted` auf `bg-base`, `surface`, `surface-muted` oder `fade-bg`. `text-muted` nicht unter 11px.
2. Pro Ansicht ein gefüllter Button (`primary-filled` mit `nav-active-text`). Gold ist keine Buttonfarbe: weißer Text erreicht darauf nur 1.8:1.
3. Status immer als Paar aus Grund und Text: Badge-Grund `*-light`, Text `*-7` (dunkel `*-3`). Das Wort steht immer im Badge.
4. Auslastung nutzt die `heat-*` Stufen, Wochensummen die `cap-*` Stufen, Risiken die `risk-*` Skala. Die Zahl steht immer in der Zelle.
5. Diagrammreihen nutzen die `chart-*` Tokens. Prognosen sind gestrichelt.
6. Löschen nur mit Bestätigungsdialog.
7. Seiteninhalt höchstens `content-max-width` breit. Die Planungsansichten füllen den Platz zwischen Navigation und rechtem Rand.
8. Neue Farben zuerst als Token in `alloq-theme.css` anlegen, hell und dunkel zusammen.

## Komponenten

Die Komponentenseiten zeigen statische Nachbauten in HTML und CSS. Die Stile stehen in `components/bundle.css` (Klassen `aq-*`) und nutzen nur Tokens.

| Gruppe | Komponenten |
| --- | --- |
| Actions | Button, ActionIcon |
| Inputs | TextInput, Select, Switch |
| Navigation | Navigation, SegmentedControl, ViewModeToggle, Tabs |
| Layout | PageHeader, Toolbar, FilterRow, FormSection |
| Data display | Badge, Avatar, Progress, DataTable |
| Cards | ProjectCard, EmployeeCard |
| Dashboard | KpiCard, CapacityCard, RiskList, ForecastChart |
| Planning | PlanningGrid, Heatmap, Gantt, RiskMatrix |
| Overlays | ModalDrawer, ConfirmDialog, UserMenu, Tooltip |
| Feedback | EmptyState |

## Not synced

- Der Seitenverlauf `--alloq-app-bg` besteht aus fünf Radialverläufen und lässt sich nicht als Token abbilden. Er steht in `assets/css/alloq-theme.css`.
- Die Radix-Variablen (`--accent-*`, `--blue-*` usw.) und die vollständigen Mantine-Skalen 0 bis 9 sind nur teilweise als Tokens übernommen.
- Die Reflex-Komponenten selbst sind nicht gebündelt. Die Vorschauen sind Nachbauten.
- Violett (`cap-tight`, Prognosen) und Blau 0 bis 1 (`cap-absent`) sind Mantine-Standardfarben und passen nicht zur gedämpften Palette.
- Einige Texte sind noch englisch („Search by name“, „Planned Value“).
- `assets/img/logo.svg` enthält ein fremdes Wortzeichen (Voyager) und wurde nicht übernommen.

"""App shell in the macOS style: translucent source-list sidebar on the left,
a floating white content pane with a toolbar on the right.

In the desktop window the native traffic lights sit on top of the sidebar
(title bar style "Overlay" in tauri.conf.json); the top row stays free for
them and, like the toolbar, drags the window.
"""

from typing import Any

import appkit_mantine as mn
import reflex as rx

from portfolio.ui import theme
from portfolio.ui.components.bank_logo import bank_logo
from portfolio.ui.components.splash import splash
from portfolio.ui.states.sidebar import SidebarBank, SidebarState

SIDEBAR_WIDTH = "252px"
# Title bar geometry (from the prototype): the traffic lights sit on one center
# line, measured from the window top. tauri.conf.json centers the native window
# buttons on it (`trafficLightPosition.y`).
TITLE_BAR_CENTER_PX = 26
PANE_GAP_PX = 8
TOOLBAR_HEIGHT_PX = 64
WINDOW_ROW_PX = 20
BANK_MARK_PX = 16
SIDEBAR_PADDING_TOP_PX = TITLE_BAR_CENTER_PX - WINDOW_ROW_PX // 2

DRAG: dict[str, Any | rx.Var] = {"data-tauri-drag-region": ""}
"""Marks an element as window title bar (Tauri drags the window from it)."""

NAV_ITEMS: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = [
    ("/", "Übersicht", "house"),
    ("/kontostaende", "Kontostände", "sheet"),
    ("/depots", "Depots", "briefcase"),
    ("/festgeld", "Festgeld", "piggy-bank"),
    ("/banken", "Banken", "landmark"),
]
BALANCES_ROUTE = NAV_ITEMS[1][0]

NO_SHRINK = {"flexShrink": "0", "whiteSpace": "nowrap"}

ROW = {
    "display": "flex",
    "alignItems": "center",
    "gap": "9px",
    "height": "32px",
    "padding": "0 10px",
    "borderRadius": "8px",
    "color": theme.SIDEBAR_TEXT,
    "textDecoration": "none",
    "cursor": "default",
}
NO_HOVER = {"color": theme.SIDEBAR_TEXT}
"""Source lists don't react to hover; rx.link would turn the text blue."""


def _window_row() -> rx.Component:
    """Free space for the native window buttons."""
    return mn.box(h=WINDOW_ROW_PX, custom_attrs=DRAG)


def _identity() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.group(
        mn.center(
            rx.icon("trending-up", size=18, stroke_width=2, color="white"),
            w=34,
            h=34,
            style={
                "borderRadius": "9px",
                "backgroundColor": theme.ACCENT,
                "boxShadow": (
                    "inset 0 0 0 0.5px rgba(255,255,255,0.35), "
                    "0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.18)"
                ),
            },
        ),
        mn.stack(
            mn.text("Portfolio", fz="14px", fw=600, c=theme.SIDEBAR_TEXT),
            mn.text(SidebarState.bank_caption, fz="11.5px", c=theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED),
            gap=0,
            miw=0,
        ),
        gap=10,
        px=6,
        wrap="nowrap",
        custom_attrs=DRAG,
    )


def _section(title: str, *rows: rx.Component) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.stack(
        mn.text(
            title,
            fz="11px",
            fw=600,
            c=theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED,
            px=10,
            pb=4,
        ),
        *rows,
        gap=2,
    )


def _nav_item(route: str, label: str, icon: str, active: bool) -> rx.Component:
    return rx.link(
        rx.icon(icon, size=16, stroke_width=1.8, color=theme.ACCENT),
        mn.text(label, fz="13px", fw=500, flex="1"),
        href=route,
        underline="none",
        _hover=NO_HOVER,
        aria_current="page" if active else None,
        style={
            **ROW,
            "backgroundColor": theme.SIDEBAR_SELECTED if active else "transparent",
        },
    )


def _bank_mark(bank: SidebarBank) -> rx.Component:
    """Logo tile, or the color dot centered in the same slot."""
    dot = mn.box(
        w=9,
        h=9,
        style={"borderRadius": "50%", "backgroundColor": bank.color},
    )
    return mn.center(
        rx.cond(bank.logo, bank_logo(bank.logo, size=BANK_MARK_PX, radius=4), dot),
        w=BANK_MARK_PX,
        h=BANK_MARK_PX,
        style={"flexShrink": "0"},
    )


def _bank_item(bank: SidebarBank) -> rx.Component:
    return rx.link(
        _bank_mark(bank),
        mn.text(bank.name, fz="13px", flex="1", miw=0, truncate="end"),
        mn.text(
            bank.amount,
            fz="12px",
            c=rx.cond(bank.negative, theme.NEGATIVE, theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED),
            style={"fontVariantNumeric": "tabular-nums"},
        ),
        href=BALANCES_ROUTE,
        underline="none",
        _hover=NO_HOVER,
        style=ROW,
    )


def _status() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.group(
        rx.icon("refresh-cw", size=13, stroke_width=2),
        mn.text(SidebarState.status, fz="11.5px"),
        gap=6,
        px=10,
        c=theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED,
        wrap="nowrap",
    )


def sidebar(active_route: str) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        _window_row(),
        _identity(),
        mn.box(
            _section(
                "Ansichten",
                *(
                    _nav_item(route, label, icon, route == active_route)
                    for route, label, icon in NAV_ITEMS
                ),
            ),
            rx.cond(
                SidebarState.has_banks,
                _section("Salden", rx.foreach(SidebarState.banks, _bank_item)),
            ),
            custom_attrs={"role": "navigation", "aria-label": "Navigation"},
            style={
                "display": "flex",
                "flexDirection": "column",
                "gap": "14px",
                "flex": "1",
                "minHeight": "0",
                "overflowY": "auto",
            },
        ),
        _status(),
        style={
            "width": SIDEBAR_WIDTH,
            "flexShrink": "0",
            "overflow": "hidden",
            "boxSizing": "border-box",
            "padding": f"{SIDEBAR_PADDING_TOP_PX}px 12px 14px",
            "display": "flex",
            "flexDirection": "column",
            "gap": "18px",
        },
    )


def page_header(
    title: str, subtitle: rx.Var[str] | str, *actions: rx.Component
) -> rx.Component:
    """Window toolbar: title and subtitle on the left, actions on the right."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.group(
            mn.stack(
                mn.title(
                    title,
                    order=1,
                    fz="18px",
                    fw=650,
                    lts="-0.015em",
                    lh="1.2",
                    c=theme.TEXT,
                    custom_attrs=DRAG,
                ),
                # mn.text(
                #     subtitle,
                #     fz="12px",
                #     lh="1.2",
                #     c=theme.TEXT_MUTED,
                #     truncate="end",
                #     custom_attrs=DRAG,
                # ),
                gap=0,
                miw=0,
                custom_attrs=DRAG,
            ),
            gap="sm",
            wrap="nowrap",
            miw=0,
            custom_attrs=DRAG,
        ),
        mn.group(*actions, gap=8, wrap="nowrap", justify="flex-end", style=NO_SHRINK),
        custom_attrs=DRAG,
        style={
            "height": f"{TOOLBAR_HEIGHT_PX}px",
            "flexShrink": "0",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "justifyContent": "space-between",
            "gap": "16px",
            "padding": "0 20px 0 24px",
            # Inset line instead of a border keeps the content centered.
            "boxShadow": f"inset 0 -1px 0 {theme.SEPARATOR}",
            "backgroundColor": theme.SURFACE,
        },
    )


def app_layout(
    header: rx.Component, *content: rx.Component, active_route: str
) -> rx.Component:
    """Window: sidebar plus floating pane with toolbar and scrolling content."""
    return mn.box(
        rx.el.style(theme.GLOBAL_CSS),
        splash(),
        sidebar(active_route),
        mn.box(
            header,
            mn.box(
                *content,
                style={
                    "flex": "1",
                    "minHeight": "0",
                    "display": "flex",
                    "flexDirection": "column",
                    "gap": "16px",
                    "padding": "22px 24px 28px",
                    "overflowY": "auto",
                    "backgroundColor": theme.BACKGROUND,
                },
            ),
            custom_attrs={"role": "main"},
            style={
                "flex": "1",
                "minWidth": "0",
                "margin": f"{PANE_GAP_PX}px {PANE_GAP_PX}px {PANE_GAP_PX}px 0",
                "display": "flex",
                "flexDirection": "column",
                "overflow": "hidden",
                "borderRadius": "16px",
                "backgroundColor": theme.SURFACE,
                "boxShadow": theme.PANE_SHADOW,
            },
        ),
        style={"display": "flex", "height": "100vh", "overflow": "hidden"},
    )
"""Design tokens and the Mantine theme: the macOS look, light and dark.

All colors live here. Components use the CSS variables (`SURFACE`, `BORDER`,
...) or the Mantine palette `blue`; the JS grid reads the same `--vm-*`
variables. `TOKENS` holds the light values, `DARK_TOKENS` the dark ones; the
system appearance picks them (`prefers-color-scheme`). The desktop window draws
the sidebar with native vibrancy; the browser shows `WINDOW_BACKGROUND` instead
(see `GLOBAL_CSS`).
"""

import appkit_mantine as mn

from portfolio.models import AccountType, AssetClass

# macOS system blue, light → dark. Shade 6 is the accent (#0071E3), shade 5 the
# dark mode accent (#0A84FF).
BLUE = [
    "#E6F1FD",
    "#CCE3FB",
    "#99C7F7",
    "#66AAF2",
    "#338EEE",
    "#0A84FF",
    "#0071E3",
    "#0062CC",
    "#004A99",
    "#003366",
]

# Chart and bank colors: the vibrant macOS system colors of the prototype, in a
# fixed order. Sidebar dots, bank tiles and chart series share them.
CHART_PALETTE = [
    "#0071E3",  # blue
    "#34C759",  # green
    "#FF9F0A",  # orange
    "#AF52DE",  # purple
    "#FF375F",  # pink
    "#5AC8FA",  # light blue
    "#8E8E93",  # gray
]
SPLASH_COLORS = (CHART_PALETTE[5], CHART_PALETTE[0], CHART_PALETTE[3])
"""Light blue, blue and purple: the three base colors of the splash gradient."""
SPLASH_BACKGROUND = (
    f"radial-gradient(88% 98% at 5% 0%, {SPLASH_COLORS[0]}66 0%, transparent 78%), "
    f"radial-gradient(78% 88% at 95% 5%, {SPLASH_COLORS[1]}3D 0%, transparent 78%), "
    f"radial-gradient(92% 98% at 80% 100%, {SPLASH_COLORS[2]}52 0%, "
    "transparent 78%), #F5F6FA"
)
"""Soft mesh of large, overlapping tinted glows on a light base: top left,
top right and bottom right."""
SPLASH_ICON_FILTER = "drop-shadow(0 10px 24px rgba(0, 40, 110, 0.18))"

WINDOW_BACKGROUND = (
    "radial-gradient(900px 600px at 0% 0%, #EDE7F3 0%, transparent 60%), "
    "radial-gradient(800px 700px at 100% 100%, #E1E8F4 0%, transparent 60%), "
    "#E9E9EE"
)
"""Browser stand-in for the native sidebar material."""

WINDOW_BACKGROUND_DARK = (
    "radial-gradient(900px 600px at 0% 0%, #2A2533 0%, transparent 60%), "
    "radial-gradient(800px 700px at 100% 100%, #222936 0%, transparent 60%), "
    "#1E1E22"
)
SPLASH_BACKGROUND_DARK = (
    f"radial-gradient(88% 98% at 5% 0%, {SPLASH_COLORS[0]}38 0%, transparent 78%), "
    f"radial-gradient(78% 88% at 95% 5%, {SPLASH_COLORS[1]}33 0%, transparent 78%), "
    f"radial-gradient(92% 98% at 80% 100%, {SPLASH_COLORS[2]}38 0%, "
    "transparent 78%), #16171B"
)
"""The same mesh, dimmer, on a dark base."""

TOKENS: dict[str, str] = {
    "background": "#FBFBFC",
    "surface": "#FFFFFF",
    "surface-muted": "#F7F7F9",
    "hover": "#F5F5F7",
    "border": "#ECECF0",
    "border-strong": "#D6D6DC",
    "separator": "#EFEFF2",
    "card-border": "#EDEDF1",
    "text": "#1D1D1F",
    "text-muted": "#6E6E73",
    "text-tertiary": "#8A8A90",
    "primary": BLUE[6],
    "link": BLUE[7],
    "sidebar-text": "#1D1D1F",
    "sidebar-muted": "rgba(29, 29, 31, 0.55)",
    "sidebar-selected": "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)",
    "sidebar-control": "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45)",
    "accent": BLUE[6],
    "positive": "#1E8E3E",
    "negative": "#D70015",
    "focus": BLUE[6],
    "selection": "rgba(0, 113, 227, 0.12)",
    "list-selected": "rgba(0, 113, 227, 0.08)",
    "label": "#5C5C62",
    "readonly": "#FAFAFB",
    "swatch-outline": "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)",
    "window-background": WINDOW_BACKGROUND,
    "pane-shadow": (
        "0 0 0 0.5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.09), 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05), "
        "0 14px 36px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)"
    ),
    "sticky-shadow": "0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.04),0 8px 16px -8px rgba(0,0,0,.24)",
    "splash-background": SPLASH_BACKGROUND,
    "splash-track": "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)",
}

DARK_TOKENS: dict[str, str] = {
    "background": "#1C1C1E",
    "surface": "#232325",
    "surface-muted": "#29292C",
    "hover": "#2C2C2F",
    "border": "#38383B",
    "border-strong": "#4A4A4E",
    "separator": "#303033",
    "card-border": "#323235",
    "text": "#F5F5F7",
    "text-muted": "#A1A1A6",
    "text-tertiary": "#7C7C82",
    "primary": BLUE[5],
    "link": "#409CFF",
    "sidebar-text": "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88)",
    "sidebar-muted": "rgba(235, 235, 245, 0.5)",
    "sidebar-selected": "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1)",
    "sidebar-control": "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)",
    "accent": BLUE[5],
    "positive": "#30D158",
    "negative": "#FF453A",
    "focus": BLUE[5],
    "selection": "rgba(10, 132, 255, 0.24)",
    "list-selected": "rgba(10, 132, 255, 0.16)",
    "label": "#A8A8AE",
    "readonly": "#262628",
    "swatch-outline": "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14)",
    "window-background": WINDOW_BACKGROUND_DARK,
    "pane-shadow": (
        "0 0 0 0.5px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1), 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3), "
        "0 14px 36px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45)"
    ),
    "sticky-shadow": "0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.3),0 8px 16px -8px rgba(0,0,0,.6)",
    "splash-background": SPLASH_BACKGROUND_DARK,
    "splash-track": "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12)",
}
"""macOS dark appearance: elevated surfaces get lighter, accents brighter."""

MANTINE_DARK = [
    "#E5E5EA",
    "#C7C7CC",
    "#98989D",
    "#6E6E73",
    "#48484A",
    "#3A3A3C",

    "#232325",
    "#1C1C1E",
    "#121214",
]
"""Neutral macOS grays for Mantine's dark scheme (7 = body = `surface`)."""


def token(name: str) -> str:
    """CSS variable reference for a token, e.g. ``var(--vm-border)``."""
    if name not in TOKENS:
        raise KeyError(name)
    return f"var(--vm-{name})"


BACKGROUND = token("background")

"""App shell in the macOS style: translucent source-list sidebar on the left,
a floating white content pane with a toolbar on the right.

In the desktop window the native traffic lights sit on top of the sidebar
(title bar style "Overlay" in tauri.conf.json); the top row stays free for
them and, like the toolbar, drags the window.
"""

from typing import Any

import appkit_mantine as mn
import reflex as rx

from portfolio.ui import theme
from portfolio.ui.components.bank_logo import bank_logo
from portfolio.ui.components.splash import splash
from portfolio.ui.states.sidebar import SidebarBank, SidebarState

SIDEBAR_WIDTH = "252px"
# Title bar geometry (from the prototype): the traffic lights sit on one center
# line, measured from the window top. tauri.conf.json centers the native window
# buttons on it (`trafficLightPosition.y`).
TITLE_BAR_CENTER_PX = 26
PANE_GAP_PX = 8
TOOLBAR_HEIGHT_PX = 64
WINDOW_ROW_PX = 20
BANK_MARK_PX = 16
SIDEBAR_PADDING_TOP_PX = TITLE_BAR_CENTER_PX - WINDOW_ROW_PX // 2

DRAG: dict[str, Any | rx.Var] = {"data-tauri-drag-region": ""}
"""Marks an element as window title bar (Tauri drags the window from it)."""

NAV_ITEMS: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = [
    ("/", "Übersicht", "house"),
    ("/kontostaende", "Kontostände", "sheet"),
    ("/depots", "Depots", "briefcase"),
    ("/festgeld", "Festgeld", "piggy-bank"),
    ("/banken", "Banken", "landmark"),
]
BALANCES_ROUTE = NAV_ITEMS[1][0]

NO_SHRINK = {"flexShrink": "0", "whiteSpace": "nowrap"}

ROW = {
    "display": "flex",
    "alignItems": "center",
    "gap": "9px",
    "height": "32px",
    "padding": "0 10px",
    "borderRadius": "8px",
    "color": theme.SIDEBAR_TEXT,
    "textDecoration": "none",
    "cursor": "default",
}
NO_HOVER = {"color": theme.SIDEBAR_TEXT}
"""Source lists don't react to hover; rx.link would turn the text blue."""


def _window_row() -> rx.Component:
    """Free space for the native window buttons."""
    return mn.box(h=WINDOW_ROW_PX, custom_attrs=DRAG)


def _identity() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.group(
        mn.center(
            rx.icon("trending-up", size=18, stroke_width=2, color="white"),
            w=34,
            h=34,
            style={
                "borderRadius": "9px",
                "backgroundColor": theme.ACCENT,
                "boxShadow": (
                    "inset 0 0 0 0.5px rgba(255,255,255,0.35), "
                    "0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.18)"
                ),
            },
        ),
        mn.stack(
            mn.text("Portfolio", fz="14px", fw=600, c=theme.SIDEBAR_TEXT),
            mn.text(SidebarState.bank_caption, fz="11.5px", c=theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED),
            gap=0,
            miw=0,
        ),
        gap=10,
        px=6,
        wrap="nowrap",
        custom_attrs=DRAG,
    )


def _section(title: str, *rows: rx.Component) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.stack(
        mn.text(
            title,
            fz="11px",
            fw=600,
            c=theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED,
            px=10,
            pb=4,
        ),
        *rows,
        gap=2,
    )


def _nav_item(route: str, label: str, icon: str, active: bool) -> rx.Component:
    return rx.link(
        rx.icon(icon, size=16, stroke_width=1.8, color=theme.ACCENT),
        mn.text(label, fz="13px", fw=500, flex="1"),
        href=route,
        underline="none",
        _hover=NO_HOVER,
        aria_current="page" if active else None,
        style={
            **ROW,
            "backgroundColor": theme.SIDEBAR_SELECTED if active else "transparent",
        },
    )


def _bank_mark(bank: SidebarBank) -> rx.Component:
    """Logo tile, or the color dot centered in the same slot."""
    dot = mn.box(
        w=9,
        h=9,
        style={"borderRadius": "50%", "backgroundColor": bank.color},
    )
    return mn.center(
        rx.cond(bank.logo, bank_logo(bank.logo, size=BANK_MARK_PX, radius=4), dot),
        w=BANK_MARK_PX,
        h=BANK_MARK_PX,
        style={"flexShrink": "0"},
    )


def _bank_item(bank: SidebarBank) -> rx.Component:
    return rx.link(
        _bank_mark(bank),
        mn.text(bank.name, fz="13px", flex="1", miw=0, truncate="end"),
        mn.text(
            bank.amount,
            fz="12px",
            c=rx.cond(bank.negative, theme.NEGATIVE, theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED),
            style={"fontVariantNumeric": "tabular-nums"},
        ),
        href=BALANCES_ROUTE,
        underline="none",
        _hover=NO_HOVER,
        style=ROW,
    )


def _status() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.group(
        rx.icon("refresh-cw", size=13, stroke_width=2),
        mn.text(SidebarState.status, fz="11.5px"),
        gap=6,
        px=10,
        c=theme.SIDEBAR_MUTED,
        wrap="nowrap",
    )


def sidebar(active_route: str) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        _window_row(),
        _identity(),
        mn.box(
            _section(
                "Ansichten",
                *(
                    _nav_item(route, label, icon, route == active_route)
                    for route, label, icon in NAV_ITEMS
                ),
            ),
            rx.cond(
                SidebarState.has_banks,
                _section("Salden", rx.foreach(SidebarState.banks, _bank_item)),
            ),
            custom_attrs={"role": "navigation", "aria-label": "Navigation"},
            style={
                "display": "flex",
                "flexDirection": "column",
                "gap": "14px",
                "flex": "1",
                "minHeight": "0",
                "overflowY": "auto",
            },
        ),
        _status(),
        style={
            "width": SIDEBAR_WIDTH,
            "flexShrink": "0",
            "overflow": "hidden",
            "boxSizing": "border-box",
            "padding": f"{SIDEBAR_PADDING_TOP_PX}px 12px 14px",
            "display": "flex",
            "flexDirection": "column",
            "gap": "18px",
        },
    )


def page_header(
    title: str, subtitle: rx.Var[str] | str, *actions: rx.Component
) -> rx.Component:
    """Window toolbar: title and subtitle on the left, actions on the right."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.group(
            mn.stack(
                mn.title(
                    title,
                    order=1,
                    fz="18px",
                    fw=650,
                    lts="-0.015em",
                    lh="1.2",
                    c=theme.TEXT,
                    custom_attrs=DRAG,
                ),
                # mn.text(
                #     subtitle,
                #     fz="12px",
                #     lh="1.2",
                #     c=theme.TEXT_MUTED,
                #     truncate="end",
                #     custom_attrs=DRAG,
                # ),
                gap=0,
                miw=0,
                custom_attrs=DRAG,
            ),
            gap="sm",
            wrap="nowrap",
            miw=0,
            custom_attrs=DRAG,
        ),
        mn.group(*actions, gap=8, wrap="nowrap", justify="flex-end", style=NO_SHRINK),
        custom_attrs=DRAG,
        style={
            "height": f"{TOOLBAR_HEIGHT_PX}px",
            "flexShrink": "0",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "justifyContent": "space-between",
            "gap": "16px",
            "padding": "0 20px 0 24px",
            # Inset line instead of a border keeps the content centered.
            "boxShadow": f"inset 0 -1px 0 {theme.SEPARATOR}",
            "backgroundColor": theme.SURFACE,
        },
    )


def app_layout(
    header: rx.Component, *content: rx.Component, active_route: str
) -> rx.Component:
    """Window: sidebar plus floating pane with toolbar and scrolling content."""
    return mn.box(
        rx.el.style(theme.GLOBAL_CSS),
        splash(),
        sidebar(active_route),
        mn.box(
            header,
            mn.box(
                *content,
                style={
                    "flex": "1",
                    "minHeight": "0",
                    "display": "flex",
                    "flexDirection": "column",
                    "gap": "16px",
                    "padding": "22px 24px 28px",
                    "overflowY": "auto",
                    "backgroundColor": theme.BACKGROUND,
                },
            ),
            custom_attrs={"role": "main"},
            style={
                "flex": "1",
                "minWidth": "0",
                "margin": f"{PANE_GAP_PX}px {PANE_GAP_PX}px {PANE_GAP_PX}px 0",
                "display": "flex",
                "flexDirection": "column",
                "overflow": "hidden",
                "borderRadius": "16px",
                "backgroundColor": theme.SURFACE,
                "boxShadow": theme.PANE_SHADOW,
            },
        ),
        style={"display": "flex", "height": "100vh", "overflow": "hidden"},
    )

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

function.description:

items.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

filePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a file to save the script output to. If omitted, the output is returned inline.

dialogAction.description: Handle dialogs while execution. "accept", "dismiss", or string for response of window.prompt. Defaults to accept.
